What Is DKIM?

DKIM (DomainKeys Identified Mail) is an email authentication method that lets a receiving server verify a message was sent by the domain it claims and was not altered in transit.

How DKIM works

The sending server signs headers with a private key. According to the RFC 6376 specification, receivers fetch the public key from DNS. Adoption reached 87% of the top 10,000 domains in 2025.

DKIM alone does not stop spoofing; pair it with SPF and DMARC.

Key rotation

Rotate keys every 6 months. See M3AAWG guidance and our DMARC guide.
